explanation: Raja Todar Mal formulated the 'Ain-i Dahsala' (10-year revenue assessment) and Zabt cash-revenue schedules.

subject: Social Science
question: Who was Akbar's close friend, courtier, and court historian who wrote the monumental three-volume official history 'Akbar Nama' and 'Ain-i Akbari'?
explanation: Abul Fazl composed the Akbar Nama (Vol 1: ancestors, Vol 2: Akbar's reign) and Vol 3: Ain-i Akbari (administration and statistics).

subject: Social Science
question: What was the philosophical doctrine of 'Universal Peace' and religious tolerance formulated by Akbar and Abul Fazl called?
explanation: Sulh-i Kul (peace with all) promoted universal religious tolerance and justice without sectarian discrimination.

subject: Social Science
question: In which hall of inter-faith discussions built at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575 did Akbar hold spiritual dialogues with theologians of diverse religions (Ulama, Brahmins, Jesuit priests, Zoroastrians)?
explanation: The Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri hosted comparative theological debates leading Akbar to develop Sulh-i Kul.

subject: Social Science
question: What was the Mughal custom of dynastic succession regarding the inheritance of royal power?
options: Coparcenary Inheritance (Timurid tradition of dividing the empire among all brothers / sons), which frequently triggered bitter wars of succession among royal princes
Strict Primogeniture (only the eldest son inherits everything)
The crown was passed to the King's uncle
explanation: The Mughals rejected strict primogeniture, adhering to Timurid coparcenary partition which sparked violent fratricidal succession wars.

subject: Social Science
question: How did Akbar build a lasting alliance with Rajput rulers (such as the Kachhwahas of Amber) to consolidate his pan-Indian empire?
options: He respected Rajput martial honor, formed marital matrimonial alliances, granted high Mansabdari military commands to Rajput chiefs, and restored conquered lands as hereditary 'Watan Jagirs'
He forced Rajputs to migrate to Iran
explanation: Akbar's Rajput policy combined diplomatic respect, matrimonial ties, high court ranks (Man Singh), and autonomy over Watan Jagirs.

subject: Social Science
question: Who was Mehr-un-Nisa (Empress Nur Jahan) and what immense political authority did she exercise during the reign of Emperor Jahangir?
options: She was Jahangir's brilliant, exceptionally influential empress who held supreme imperial power, issued royal farmans (orders), and had coins minted jointly in her name alongside the Emperor
She was a court poetess with no political power
She lived in exile outside India
She was the ruler of Bengal
explanation: Nur Jahan exercised supreme administrative co-sovereignty, issuing sovereign farmans and appearing on imperial coinage.

subject: Social Science
question: What was the administrative division of the Mughal Empire under Akbar?
options: The empire was divided into Subas (provinces) governed by a Subadar ; each Suba was subdivided into Sarkars (districts) and Parganas (sub-districts/parishes)
The empire was divided into 100 kingdoms
The empire was divided into two halves: North and South
explanation: Suba (governed by Subadar and financial Diwan) → Sarkar (district under Faujdar) → Pargana (under Shiqdar and Amil) → Grama.

subject: Social Science
question: In Mughal provincial administration, who were the 'Subadar' and the 'Diwan' of a province (Suba)?
options: The Subadar carried out political and military functions ; the Diwan was the financial officer responsible for revenue collection and accounting
The Subadar was a doctor ; the Diwan was a teacher
The Diwan was the supreme general and Subadar was the cook
explanation: Mughal checks-and-balances: executive-military authority resided in the Subadar; fiscal-financial authority resided independently in the Diwan.

subject: Social Science
question: What was the 'Zabt' revenue system formulated by Todar Mal?
options: A scientific revenue system where agricultural land was physically surveyed/measured, crop yields and market price indices over 10 years were calculated, and each crop was assigned a fixed cash revenue tax schedule
A system where soldiers took all food by force
A tax only on foreign traders
explanation: Zabt established empirical crop-specific cash schedules based on standard land measurement (bigha/jarib) and 10-year price averages.

subject: Social Science
question: In Mughal society, what blanket umbrella term was used to describe all rural intermediaries—whether powerful local village headmen (Muqaddams/Chaudhuris) or hereditary regional chieftains?
explanation: The Mughals employed 'Zamindar' generically for all rural landed intermediaries collecting agricultural surplus.

subject: Social Science
question: Why did the Sisodiya Rajputs of Mewar refuse to accept Mughal authority for a long time, and how did the Mughals treat them when they finally surrendered to Jahangir in 1614?
options: Mewar resisted fiercely under Maharana Pratap ; upon submission under Rana Amar Singh, Jahangir treated them with honorable nobility, returning their entire territory as a Watan Jagir
Jahangir annexed Mewar and destroyed its forts
Mewar was given to foreign merchants
explanation: Jahangir preserved Sisodiya dignity by restoring Mewar as a hereditary Watan Jagir exempt from personal court attendance.

subject: Social Science
question: Why did Aurangzeb's long, grinding 25-year military campaigns in the Deccan (1681–1707) lead to the severe exhaustion and eventual decline of the Mughal Empire?
options: Endless Deccan wars drained imperial treasuries, overextended military logistics, sparked protracted guerilla warfare with Marathas, and caused the collapse of administrative supervision in the northern heartland
Because Aurangzeb gave up his empire to become a monk
Because the Deccan had no soldiers
Because the British invaded Delhi in 1682
explanation: Aurangzeb's Deccan ulcer drained the empire's fiscal resources, disrupted Jagirdari stability, and triggered administrative paralysis.

subject: Social Science
question: What was the 'Jagirdari Crisis' that crippled the Mughal administration in the late 17th century under Aurangzeb?
options: The massive inflation in the number of Mansabdars created a severe shortage of productive Jagirs; Jagirdars ruthlessly squeezed peasants for maximum revenue during their brief assignments
All Jagirs were destroyed by floods
Jagirs were banned by imperial law
explanation: Shortage of revenue-bearing paibaqi land caused the Jagirdari crisis, triggering agrarian distress and peasant rebellions.

subject: Social Science
question: Which Maratha warrior king established an independent Maratha kingdom, using brilliant guerilla warfare (Ganimi Kava) against Aurangzeb's armies and escaped from house arrest in Agra in 1666?
explanation: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj forged an autonomous Maratha swarajya, defying Mughal hegemony via mobile guerrilla tactics.

subject: Social Science
question: What is the third volume of Abul Fazl's Akbar Nama called, which contains rich statistical details about crops, yields, prices, wages, administrative regulations, and cultural traditions?
explanation: The Ain-i Akbari constitutes the definitive imperial gazetteer and administrative-statistical compendium of Akbar's reign.

subject: Social Science
question: Which Mughal prince translated fifty Upanishads from Sanskrit into Persian ('Sirr-i Akbar' / The Greatest Secret), appreciating the unity of divine truth across Hinduism and Islam?
options: Dara Shikoh (eldest son of Shah Jahan)
explanation: Dara Shikoh was a philosopher-prince who translated the Upanishads and authored 'Majma-ul-Bahrain' (Mingling of Two Oceans).

subject: Social Science
question: What was the 'Kotwal' in Mughal urban municipal administration?
options: The chief town police officer responsible for urban law and order, night patrols, market surveillance, and citizen registry
The head priest of the mosque
explanation: The Kotwal exercised municipal police, judicial oversight, market weights inspection, and urban safety policing.

subject: Social Science
question: Which rebellious son of Aurangzeb received military support from the Marathas and the Deccan Sultanate before fleeing to Safavid Iran in 1681?
explanation: Prince Akbar revolted against his father Aurangzeb in 1681, allied with Sambhaji, and sought refuge with the Safavid Shah of Persia.

subject: Social Science
question: What magnificent white marble mausoleum did Emperor Shah Jahan construct in Agra along the Yamuna river in memory of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal?
options: The Taj Mahal (built between 1632 and 1648 CE)
explanation: The Taj Mahal is the supreme masterpiece of Indo-Islamic symmetry, Pietra Dura inlay, and domed architectural engineering.

subject: Social Science
question:
Read the statements:
Assertion (A): The Mughal Mansabdari system was a remarkably dynamic, non-hereditary administrative hierarchy that integrated diverse ethnic elites (Turanians, Iranis, Rajputs, Indian Muslims, and Marathas) into a unified imperial ruling class.
Reason (R): Mansabdars did not hold permanent hereditary property rights over their Jagirs; they were subjected to regular transfers, strict military muster reviews (Dagh and Chehra), and post-mortem escheat of property to the crown.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: Akbar's genius lay in institutionalizing an ethnically diverse, meritocratic, non-hereditary administrative elite loyal to the central sovereign.

subject: Social Science
question:
Spot the IMPOSTER in the following chronological sequence of Mughal Emperors and their major architectural/political milestones:
Group:
1. Babur - Founded empire, laid out formal Persian Charbagh gardens
2. Akbar - Built Fatehpur Sikri, Agra Fort, instituted Sulh-i Kul
3. Shah Jahan - Built Taj Mahal, Red Fort Delhi, Jama Masjid
4. Aurangzeb - Built the Eiffel Tower in Delhi
options: Milestone 4 (The Eiffel Tower is in Paris, France ; Aurangzeb built Moti Masjid and Badshahi Mosque)
explanation: Milestone 4 is an absurd falsehood: Aurangzeb built the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore and Moti Masjid in Delhi, not the Eiffel Tower.

subject: Social Science
question:
Analyze the fiscal disparity in the Mughal Empire revealed in official records:
Out of 8,000 Mansabdars under Shah Jahan, only 445 top-ranking officers (a mere 5.6% of the nobility) received what percentage of the empire's total assessed revenue?
options: 61.5% of the total estimated revenue of the empire was concentrated in the hands of this tiny elite of 445 nobles
explanation: Official Mughal records show extreme economic inequality: 5.6% of top-tier Mansabdars appropriated 61.5% of state revenues for salaries.

subject: Social Science
question:
Match Column I (Mughal Administrative Terms) with Column II (Exact Functional Meanings):
(a) Subadar -> (i) Provincial governor commanding political and military administration
(b) Diwan   -> (ii) Provincial chief revenue and finance officer
(c) Bakhshi -> (iii) Imperial military paymaster responsible for troop muster
(d) Sadr    -> (iv) Minister in charge of religious and charitable patronage
explanation: Subadar = governor; Diwan = finance; Bakhshi = military paymaster; Sadr = ecclesiastical/charitable minister.

subject: Social Science
question:
Read the statements regarding Akbar's religious policy:
Statement 1: Akbar abolished the discriminatory 'Jizya' tax on non-Muslim subjects and the pilgrimage tax on Hindu pilgrims in 1564.
Statement 2: The Ibadat Khana discussions convinced Akbar that religious bigots who emphasize ritual dogma create social division, prompting him to formulate 'Sulh-i Kul'.
Statement 3: Akbar forced all citizens of India to convert to his personal faith under penalty of death.
Which statements are TRUE?
explanation: Statement 3 is false: Akbar championed Sulh-i Kul (universal tolerance) and never enforced forced religious conversions. Statements 1 and 2 are true.

subject: Social Science
question: Why did the Mughals prefer not to be called 'Moghol / Mongol' and took great pride in their 'Timurid' paternal lineage?
options: The name Mongol was historically associated with Genghis Khan's brutal massacres of countless innocent people, whereas their ancestor Timur had captured Delhi in 1398 with great royal prestige
Because Timur was a European king
Because Babur could not speak Persian
explanation: The dynasty distanced itself from the gory memory of Genghisid massacres, glorifying their Timurid renaissance patrimony.

subject: Social Science
question: How did the introduction of Field Artillery (cannons and matchlocks) revolutionize military warfare in India during Babur's 1526 Panipat campaign?
options: Babur combined gunpowder artillery carts (Rumi device) with rapid flanking cavalry maneuvers (Tulghuma), completely decimating Ibrahim Lodi's massive static war elephant army
Artillery destroyed all food in India
Cannons were made of wood and burned down
explanation: Babur deployed Ottoman tactical innovation: chaining baggage wagons to shield matchlock gunners, supported by deadly flanking cavalry encirclement (Tulghuma).

subject: Social Science
question: What was the structural relationship between the Mughal Emperor, the Zamindars, and the Peasantry?
options: Peasants produced the agrarian wealth; Zamindars collected the produce and shared local caste/lineage ties with peasants, occasionally leading armed peasant rebellions against excessive central Mughal tax demands
Zamindars gave all their land to the Emperor for free
Peasants were paid salaries in gold by the Emperor
There were no taxes in the Mughal Empire
explanation: Local Zamindars held traditional kinship ties with village cultivators; imperial over-exploitation frequently triggered joint agrarian revolts.

subject: Social Science
question:
Consider four key regions that mounted fierce resistance against Mughal expansion in the 17th century:
1. Marathas (Deccan)
2. Ahoms (Assam/Brahmaputra Valley)
3. Sikhs (Punjab)
4. Rathores / Sisodiyas (Mewar & Marwar)
What common socio-political strategy did these regional powers employ?
options: They leveraged rugged regional terrain, intense local community cohesion, and decentralized mobile warfare to resist centralized imperial domination
They allied with the British against the Mughals
They abandoned their lands and moved to Central Asia
explanation: Regional powers mobilized geographic terrain, martial traditions, and asymmetric resistance against Mughal over-centralization.

subject: Social Science
question: Why is Abul Fazl's 'Ain-i Akbari' celebrated by modern socio-economic historians as a pioneering masterwork of statistical administration?
options: It provides rigorous empirical statistical surveys of agricultural revenue, price tables, daily wages, military rolls, fauna, flora, and socio-religious traditions across all 15 Subas of Akbar's empire
It is a fictional novel of magic and fantasy
It was written in modern English
It contains no numbers or records
explanation: The Ain-i Akbari is a landmark in quantitative historiography, offering quantitative demographic, agricultural, and administrative inventories.

subject: Social Science
question: What architectural innovation distinguishes the 'Charbagh' (Four-Gardens) layout perfected by Mughal emperors (e.g. Humayun's Tomb, Shalimar Gardens)?
options: A grand rectangular walled enclosure divided into four symmetrical quadrangles by intersecting, axial raised artificial water channels and walkways, symbolizing the four rivers of Paradise
A garden with only four flowers
A circular maze made of glass
explanation: Charbagh architecture geometricizes Persian paradise garden symbology: quadripartite orthogonal grids bisected by flowing water channels.

subject: Social Science
question: What overarching historical legacy defines Chapter 4 of NCERT Class 7 History regarding the Mughal Empire?
options: The creation of a pan-Indian empire that established enduring administrative frameworks, standardized revenue and coinage systems, synthesized composite Indo-Islamic art and architecture, and promoted cultural pluralism under Sulh-i Kul
A period of constant darkness with no administration
The complete end of all Indian culture
An empire that lasted only two weeks
explanation: Chapter 4 synthesizes the political institutionalization, fiscal centralization, architectural elegance, and cultural pluralism of the Mughal Empire.

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: वे शब्दांश जो किसी मूल शब्द के पहले (आरंभ में) जुड़कर उसके अर्थ में परिवर्तन या विशेषता ला देते हैं, उन्हें व्याकरण में क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: उप + सर्ग: मूल शब्द के पूर्व में जुड़कर अर्थ बदलने वाले सार्थक शब्दांश 'उपसर्ग' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: वे शब्दांश जो किसी मूल शब्द के अंत (पीछे) में जुड़कर नए शब्द का निर्माण करते हैं और उसके अर्थ में विशेषता लाते हैं, उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: प्रति + अय: शब्दों के अंत में जुड़कर नया अर्थ उत्पन्न करने वाले शब्दांश 'प्रत्यय' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: हिंदी में प्रयुक्त उपसर्गों को मुख्य रूप से कितने वर्गों में बाँटा गया है?
options: तीन प्रमुख वर्गों में (1. संस्कृत के तत्सम उपसर्ग, 2. हिंदी के तद्भव उपसर्ग, 3. उर्दू-फ़ारसी के विदेशी उपसर्ग)
explanation: उपसर्गों के 3 मुख्य स्रोत हैं: संस्कृत (तत्सम), हिंदी (तद्भव), तथा उर्दू-फ़ारसी (आगत)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'अति' (संस्कृत उपसर्ग - अर्थ: अधिक/परे) से बना शुद्ध शब्द कौन-सा है?
explanation: अति + अधिक = अत्यधिक (यण संधि के साथ 'अति' उपसर्ग का प्रयोग)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'प्र' उपसर्ग (अर्थ: अधिक/आगे) से बने शब्दों का सही समूह कौन-सा है?
explanation: प्र + हार = प्रहार, प्र + गति = प्रगति, प्र + बल = प्रबल।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: हिंदी के तद्भव उपसर्ग 'अ' / 'अन' (अर्थ: अभाव/निषेध) से बने शब्दों का सही उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
explanation: अ + काल = अकाल; अन + पढ़ = अनपढ़; अन + जान = अनजान।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: उर्दू-फ़ारसी उपसर्ग 'बे' (अर्थ: बिना / रहित) से बने शब्दों का सही समूह कौन-सा है?
explanation: बे + कसूर = बेकसूर, बे + इमान = बेइमान, बे + परवाह = बेपरवाह।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: प्रत्यय के मुख्य रूप से कितने भेद होते हैं?
options: दो भेद (1. कृत / कृदंत प्रत्यय - क्रिया/धातु के अंत में, 2. तद्धित प्रत्यय - संज्ञा/सर्वनाम/विशेषण के अंत में)
explanation: प्रत्यय के दो मूल भेद हैं: कृत प्रत्यय (धातु/क्रिया के साथ) तथा तद्धित प्रत्यय (संज्ञा/सर्वनाम/विशेषण के साथ)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: क्रिया की मूल धातु के अंत में जुड़कर संज्ञा या विशेषण शब्द बनाने वाले प्रत्यय क्या कहलाते हैं?
options: कृत प्रत्यय / कृदंत (जैसे: लिख् + आवट = लिखावट, पढ़् + आकू = पढ़ाकू)
explanation: धातु/क्रिया के अंत में प्रयुक्त प्रत्यय 'कृत प्रत्यय' तथा निर्मित शब्द 'कृदंत' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: संज्ञा, सर्वनाम और विशेषण शब्दों के अंत में जुड़कर नए शब्द बनाने वाले प्रत्यय क्या कहलाते हैं?
options: तद्धित प्रत्यय (जैसे: मानव + ता = मानवता, मीठा + आस = मिठास)
explanation: संज्ञा, सर्वनाम व विशेषण में जुड़ने वाले प्रत्यय 'तद्धित' तथा निर्मित शब्द 'तद्धितांत' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'मिठास' शब्द में मूल शब्द और प्रत्यय क्या है?
explanation: विशेषण 'मीठा' में भाववाचक तद्धित प्रत्यय 'आस' जुड़ने से 'मिठास' बनता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'लिखावट' शब्द में कौन-सा प्रत्यय प्रयुक्त हुआ है?
explanation: लिख् धातु में भाववाचक कृत प्रत्यय 'आवट' जुड़ने से 'लिखावट' शब्द बनता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'दुर्' (संस्कृत उपसर्ग - अर्थ: बुरा/कठिन) से बने शब्दों का सही समूह कौन-सा है?
explanation: दुर् + लभ = दुर्लभ; दुर् + आचार = दुराचार; दुर् + गम = दुर्गम; दुर् + बल = दुर्बल।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'सम्' (संस्कृत उपसर्ग - अर्थ: अच्छी तरह / पूर्णता) से बने शब्दों का सही उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
explanation: सम् + मान = सम्मान; सम् + तोष = संतोष (अनुस्वार रूप); सम् + कार = संस्कार।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'अभि' उपसर्ग (अर्थ: सामने/श्रेष्ठ) से बने शब्दों का सही समूह कौन-सा है?
explanation: अभि + मान = अभिमान; अभि + नय = अभिनय; अभि + वादन = अभिवादन।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: हिंदी के उपसर्ग 'कु' (अर्थ: बुरा) से बने शब्दों का सही समूह कौन-सा है?
explanation: कु + पुत्र = कुपुत्र; कु + संगति = कुसंगति; कु + रूप = कुरूप।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: उर्दू-फ़ारसी उपसर्ग 'कम' (अर्थ: थोड़ा/हीन) से बने शब्दों का सही उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
explanation: कम + ज़ोर = कमज़ोर; कम + अक्ल = कमअक्ल; कम + उम्र = कमउम्र।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: उर्दू-फ़ारसी उपसर्ग 'ला' (अर्थ: बिना / रहित) से बने शब्दों का सही समूह कौन-सा है?
explanation: ला + परवाह = लापरवाह; ला + वारिस = लावारिस; ला + जवाब = लाजवाब।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'इक' प्रत्यय जुड़ने पर मूल शब्द के प्रथम स्वर में होने वाले दीर्घीकरण का सही उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
options: समाज + इक = सामाजिक ; इतिहास + इक = ऐतिहासिक ; भूगोल + इक = भौगोलिक ; धर्म + इक = धार्मिक
explanation: 'इक' प्रत्यय आदि-स्वर वृद्धि करता है: अ→आ (सामाजिक), इ→ऐ (ऐतिहासिक), उ→औ (भौगोलिक)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'इत' प्रत्यय से बने शब्दों का सही समूह कौन-सा है?
options: हर्षित (हर्ष + इत), शिक्षित (शिक्षा + इत), फलित (फल + इत), पुष्पित (पुष्प + इत)
explanation: हर्ष + इत = हर्षित; शिक्षा + इत = शिक्षित; पुष्प + इत = पुष्पित।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'ता' भाववाचक तद्धित प्रत्यय से बने शब्दों का सही समूह कौन-सा है?
explanation: मानव + ता = मानवता; सुंदर + ता = सुंदरता; कटु + ता = कटुता।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'वान' और 'वती' प्रत्यय से बने शब्दों का सही उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
options: धनवान / धनवती, बलवान / बलवती, रूपवान / रूपवती
explanation: धन + वान = धनवान (पुल्लिंग) / धनवती (स्त्रीलिंग)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'वाला' कर्तृवाचक प्रत्यय से बने शब्दों का सही समूह कौन-सा है?
explanation: संज्ञा + वाला = कर्ता सूचक शब्द (दूधवाला, फलवाला)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'घबराहट' शब्द में मूल शब्द और प्रत्यय का सही विग्रह क्या है?
explanation: घबराना क्रिया की धातु में भाववाचक कृत प्रत्यय 'आहट' जुड़कर 'घबराहट' बनता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: निम्नलिखित में से किस शब्द में उपसर्ग और प्रत्यय दोनों का एक साथ प्रयोग हुआ है?
explanation: अप (उपसर्ग) + मान (मूल शब्द) + इत (प्रत्यय) = अपमानित।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: निम्नलिखित में से किस शब्द में उपसर्ग और प्रत्यय दोनों प्रयुक्त हुए हैं?
explanation: अ (उपसर्ग) + लोक (मूल शब्द) + इक (प्रत्यय) = अलौकिक।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'परोपकार' शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग प्रयुक्त हुआ है?
options: पर (पर + उपकार = परोपकार, गुण संधि के साथ)
explanation: पर (दूसरा) + उपकार = परोपकार (अ + उ = ओ, गुण संधि)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'प्रत्येक' शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग प्रयुक्त हुआ है?
options: प्रति (प्रति + एक = प्रत्येक, यण संधि के साथ)
explanation: प्रति + एक = प्रत्येक (इ + ए = ये, यण संधि)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
कथन और कारण को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़ें:
कथन (A): उपसर्ग और प्रत्यय स्वतंत्र शब्द नहीं होते, बल्कि वे भाषा के 'शब्दांश' (Bound Morphemes) होते हैं।
कारण (R): उपसर्ग और प्रत्यय का वाक्य में स्वतंत्र रूप से कोई प्रयोग नहीं किया जा सकता ; वे सदा किसी सार्थक मूल शब्द के साथ जुड़कर ही नया अर्थ प्रदान करते हैं।
सही विकल्प चुनें:
options: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
(A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता।
explanation: उपसर्ग व प्रत्यय बद्ध रूपिम (Bound Morphemes) हैं जिनका स्वतंत्र अस्तित्व नहीं होता।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
Spot the IMPOSTER in the following group of उपसर्ग और उनसे बने शब्दों में:
Group:
1. सम् - संवाद, संहार, संस्कार
2. अनु - अनुवाद, अनुकरण, अनुशासन
3. निर् - निर्मल, निर्दोष, निर्धन
4. अति - अनादर, अनहोनी, अनजान
options: युग्म 4 (अनादर, अनहोनी में 'अन् / अन' उपसर्ग है, 'अति' नहीं)
explanation: युग्म 4 में 'अन्' (अन्+आदर=अनादर) तथा 'अन' उपसर्ग हैं; 'अति' के शब्द 'अत्यंत, अत्यधिक' होते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
सुमेलित कीजिए (उपसर्ग और उनके अर्थ):
(क) उत् / उद् -> (i) ऊपर, श्रेष्ठ, ऊँचा (जैसे: उत्कर्ष, उन्नति)
(ख) दुर् / दुस् -> (ii) बुरा, कठिन, दुष्ट (जैसे: दुर्जन, दुस्साहस)
(ग) परा       -> (iii) विपरीत, पीछे, नाश (जैसे: पराजय, पराभव)
(घ) प्रति     -> (iv) प्रत्येक, सामने, विरुद्ध (जैसे: प्रतिकूल, प्रतिध्वनि)
explanation: उत् = ऊँचा; दुर् = बुरा; परा = विपरीत/पराजय; प्रति = प्रत्येक/सामने।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: निम्नलिखित में से किस शब्द में 'निर्' उपसर्ग प्रयुक्त हुआ है?
explanation: निर् + आकार = निराकार; निर् + अपराध = निरपराध (नियम/निबंध में 'नि' उपसर्ग है)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'उन्नति' शब्द का शुद्ध उपसर्ग-विच्छेद क्या होगा?
options: उत् + नति (व्यंजन संधि के नियमानुसार 'त्' का 'न्' में परिवर्तन)
explanation: उत् + नति = उन्नति (त् के बाद न आने पर त् का न् हो जाता है)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: निम्नलिखित में से किस शब्द में 'कु' उपसर्ग नहीं लगा है?
options: 'कुसुम' (क्योंकि यह एक रूढ़ मूल शब्द है, इसमें 'कु' उपसर्ग नहीं है)
explanation: 'कुसुम' (फूल) रूढ़ मूल शब्द है; बाकी तीनों में 'कु' (बुरा) उपसर्ग है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'ऐतिहासिक' और 'वैधानिक' शब्दों में मूल शब्द और प्रत्यय क्या हैं?
options: इतिहास + इक = ऐतिहासिक ; विधान + इक = वैधानिक
explanation: 'इक' प्रत्यय से इ→ऐ (इतिहास→ऐतिहासिक) तथा इ→ऐ (विधान→वैधानिक)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: निम्नलिखित में से किस शब्द में दो उपसर्गों का एक साथ प्रयोग हुआ है?
options: 'पर्यावरण' (परि + आ + वरण = पर्यावरण) और 'असुरक्षित' (अ + सु + रक्षित)
explanation: पर्यावरण = परि + आ + वरण (दो उपसर्ग); असुरक्षित = अ + सु + रक्षित (दो उपसर्ग)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: निम्नलिखित में से किस शब्द में दो प्रत्ययों का एक साथ प्रयोग हुआ है?
explanation: राष्ट्र + ईय = राष्ट्रीय + ता = राष्ट्रीयता (दो तद्धित प्रत्ययों का क्रमिक संयोग)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'सदाचार' और 'सज्जन' शब्दों में कौन-सा संस्कृत उपसर्ग प्रयुक्त हुआ है?
options: 'सत्' उपसर्ग (सत् + आचार = सदाचार ; सत् + जन = सज्जन)
explanation: संस्कृत तत्सम उपसर्ग 'सत्' (सत्+आचार=सदाचार, सत्+जन=सज्जन)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: उर्दू-फ़ारसी के उपसर्ग 'ना' (अर्थ: अभाव/नहीं) से बने शब्दों का शुद्ध समूह कौन-सा है?
explanation: ना + लायक = नालायक; ना + पसंद = नापसंद; ना + बालिग = नाबालिग।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: उपसर्ग और प्रत्यय (Affixation) के सम्यक अध्ययन का हिंदी भाषा की शब्द-रचना में क्या सर्वोच्च योगदान है?
options: यह सीमित मूल शब्दों से सहस्रों नवीन, सूक्ष्म, भावपूर्ण और पारिभाषिक शब्दों के सृजन की अद्भुत वैज्ञानिक सामर्थ्य प्रदान करता है, जिससे भाषा का शब्द-भंडार अनंत रूप से समृद्ध होता है
यह शब्दों को छोटा करने का एकमात्र तरीका है
इसका व्याकरण में कोई विशेष प्रयोग नहीं है
यह केवल परीक्षा में एक अंक के लिए पढ़ा जाता है
explanation: उपसर्ग और प्रत्यय शब्द-निर्माण की सर्वाधिक उर्वर रचनात्मक प्रविधियाँ हैं जो भाषा की शब्द-संपदा का असीमित विस्तार करती हैं।
